recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No further core source work is recommended for FHIR-14951 because the active Search page already conveys the approved warning and its later clarifications.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive FHIR-core search change request for STU3 asking to add a Chained Parameters warning that chained parameters are applied independently to the target resource, using Patient?general-practitioner.name=Joe&general-practitioner.address-state=MN as the example where different practitioners can satisfy the two criteria.
initial_application: Applied by git-svn commit 066d5651b05bedffe21a1fc177387289d1a81e5e, 'GF#14951 - note about chained searches + fix build', corresponding to the Jira comment 'svn revision 13412'. The commit added the warning paragraph, general-practitioner example, and Composite/_filter alternatives to source/search.html.
additional_context: source/hierarchy.xml lists search.html under RESTful API, confirming the inspected Search page is in current build scope. Later same-family issues refined but did not reverse the rule: FHIR-34023 clarified the example for R5 and is already represented on the combined branch, and FHIR-52942 later expanded the explanation for R6 after Zulip implementer confusion.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current source/search.html states that chained parameters are evaluated individually, that a Patient seeing Dr. Joe in California and Dr. Jane in Minnesota matches, that implementations find separate Patient sets and join them with AND at the Patient level, and that Composite search parameters or _filter are alternatives when grouped joins are required.
